title: Initiative: Audit log schema standardization + sensitive-action coverage
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Goal
Standardize audit logging across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments by (1) publishing a canonical, versioned audit event schema (v1) and (2) reaching 100% coverage for an agreed “sensitive actions” inventory. This initiative unblocks multiple active enterprise deals where “SOC 2-style audit logs” + exportability + completeness guarantees are procurement requirements.

Background / why now
We currently have partial and inconsistent audit logs across services (gateway, console backend, RBAC/auth, deployment controllers, private installer, exporter). Enterprise security reviews are increasingly asking:
- “Do you log all admin/security actions?”
- “Is there a stable schema we can map to controls?”
- “Can we export to our SIEM reliably (S3/webhook/Splunk)?”
- “What’s your delivery lag / drop behavior, and how do you prove coverage?”

In-scope (definition of sensitive actions)
Actions that materially impact customer data access, security posture, billing, or availability, including:
- Auth/RBAC changes (roles, permissions, assignments)
- API key creation/rotation/revocation
- User/admin lifecycle (invite, deactivate, role changes)
- Org/workspace settings changes (SSO toggles, allowlists, etc.)
- Model deployment + rollout actions (pin/unpin versions, canary start/stop, fallback policy)
- Routing policy changes
- Dedicated capacity scaling and quota/admin changes
- Private deployment install/upgrade/rollback
- Data retention changes
- Audit log configuration changes (export sinks, retention, filtering)

Out of scope (for initial GA)
- Non-sensitive observability events (performance/debug)
- Full historical backfill of legacy logs (only limited migration/backfill required for contract commitments)
- Customer-specific custom event formats (we will provide schema v1 + export formats; customization is a later program)

Deliverables
1) Schema v1 (canonical + versioned)
- Required fields: event_name, schema_version, occurred_at, actor model, target model, org/workspace context, request correlation (request_id/trace_id), ip/user_agent capture guidance, outcome + error semantics.
- Backwards-compat rules and versioning strategy (minor additions vs breaking changes).
- Examples for each event family (api.*, console.*, rbac.*, deploy.*, dedicated.*, private.*).

2) Shared libraries + enforcement
- Library to emit events consistently (helper types for actor/target/outcome).
- Validation (JSONSchema) in pipeline and/or service boundary, and build-time registry to prevent unregistered event names.
- Redaction rules: no secrets/tokens; guardrails for PII.

3) Sensitive actions inventory + mapping
- Single master inventory of sensitive actions and mapping to expected audit events.
- Owner per action family and subsystem.
- Coverage status and a path to 100% (with explicit exceptions policy).

4) Reliability and export readiness
- Delivery lag SLO and alerting.
- Exporter hardening: retries/backoff, DLQ, per-sink metrics.
- Export destinations for enterprise: S3 and webhook in beta; Splunk path confirmed in packaging ticket (PM-414).

Success metrics (GA)
- Coverage: 100% of “sensitive actions” inventory mapped to at least one event, and verified via automated integration tests.
- Schema stability: schema v1 published and referenced by Console UI and export docs; backward-compat policy approved by Security + GRC.
- Reliability: meet delivery lag SLO for 30 days in production (definition and thresholds finalized with SRE).
- Export: at least one enterprise design partner successfully ingesting into SIEM from Redwood export with documented runbook.

Milestones & timeline (targeting 2 quarters)
Phase 1 — Discovery + inventory (Target: 2–3 weeks)
- Enumerate sensitive actions across subsystems; agree on definition and boundaries.
- Audit existing logs and identify gaps.
- Output: Inventory doc + acceptance criteria for “100% coverage.”

Phase 2 — Schema v1 + libraries (Target: 3–5 weeks)
- Publish schema v1 + naming guidelines.
- Implement validator + event registry + initial developer guidance.
- Output: Confluence spec + library in place for early adopters.

Phase 3 — Instrumentation + migration (Target: 6–10 weeks)
- Service-by-service instrumentation.
- Legacy normalization (dual-write / rename map) where required.
- Output: majority of action families covered; integration test harness running in staging.

Phase 4 — Reliability + reporting (Target: 3–6 weeks)
- Delivery lag SLO, dashboards, alerts.
- Coverage scanner + CI gate.
- Exporter reliability (DLQ, per-sink metrics) and operational runbook.

Phase 5 — Beta + launch (Target: 3–6 weeks)
- 3–5 enterprise design partners enabled.
- Security review collateral (FAQ + PRD alignment) and internal operator training.
- GA with documented schema guarantees + support runbooks.

Release plan (proposed)
- Internal Alpha: schema v1 + library available; limited instrumentation (API keys + RBAC); export to internal sink only.
- Private Beta (design partners): S3 + webhook exports; Console Audit Logs UI (read-only) behind feature flag; coverage scanner reporting enabled.
- GA: coverage gates enforced for new sensitive actions; exporter SLO + alerting live; customer-facing docs/FAQ published.

Beta criteria (must-have)
- Schema v1 published and frozen (no breaking changes during beta).
- Coverage minimum for beta: API key lifecycle + RBAC changes + one deployment family (model rollout OR dedicated scaling OR private upgrade) end-to-end, including correlation IDs and actor attribution.
- Export reliability: retried delivery + DLQ; documented failure behavior; ability to replay from persisted store.
- Access controls: Audit Logs API/UI restricted to admin roles; internal access policy documented.

GA acceptance criteria (must-have)
- 100% sensitive action coverage achieved OR explicit exceptions approved by Security Eng + CISO delegate + GRC (with documented compensating controls).
- CI enforcement: block merges that introduce new sensitive actions without inventory mapping + event registration.
- Integration tests: representative actions per subsystem assert presence + required fields.
- Delivery lag SLO met for 30 days; paging policy and runbook tested.
- Redaction policy implemented and verified (no secrets/tokens; reviewed IP/user-agent retention guidance).

Cross-team commitments (current owners)
- Product/Program: Naomi Feldman (PO), Talia Benson (program management), Elliot Price (publication/docs).
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin (schema + enforcement requirements), Dr. Aisha Rahman (exec sponsor).
- GRC: Olga Petrov (SOC 2/ISO mapping + evidence expectations).
- Platform/Telemetry: Nadia Rahman (pipeline instrumentation), Mei Lin (coverage datasets/scanner), Allison Grant (observability standards).
- SRE: Rafael Mendes + Miles Thornton (delivery lag SLO, alerts/runbooks), Sean Gallagher (operations readiness).
- Console: Dylan Brooks + Chloe Martin (Audit Logs API), Felix Schneider (UI).
- Private: Vivek Kulkarni + Bruno Silva (installer/upgrade auditing).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Actor attribution for controller-initiated actions: when runtime/controller acts on behalf of a user, define actor.service vs actor.user and required “initiator” fields.
- Data minimization: IP/user-agent retention by deployment mode (Hosted vs Private) and redaction defaults; legal guidance required for enterprise default settings.
- Export packaging: which sinks are included in base enterprise vs add-on; retention tiers and pricing (tracked in PM-414).

Risks
- Fragmented ownership across subsystems causing partial coverage and inconsistent “done” definitions.
- Performance concerns leading to requests for sampling (not acceptable for audit logs); must align early.
- Legacy event names and migration complexity impacting customers consuming early logs.

Links / references
- Confluence (drafts): Audit Logging Program Overview; Audit Event Schema v1; Sensitive Actions Inventory; Coverage Policy and Enforcement; Threat Model; Legacy Migration Plan; SOC2 Control Mapping; Telemetry Standards.
- Related tickets: PM-413 (beta program), PM-414 (packaging), DES-133 (Console UX), ENG-2481..ENG-2493 (engineering workstreams).

Comms plan
- Weekly cross-team sync (Security + Telemetry + SRE + Console + Private) with a single source-of-truth coverage dashboard.
- Monthly enterprise readiness update to Sales/SE and Security review collateral checkpoint.

Owner next steps (this week)
- Finalize milestone dates + beta entry criteria in PM-413.
- Confirm schema v1 required fields and naming guideline decisions with Security Eng.
- Publish initial inventory template and owners per subsystem; start gap audit by service.
